chosen.premise: During storms, Electabuzz competes to climb lightning-prone heights, and some towns use it as a lightning rod.
chosen.hook: When lightning comes, Electabuzz races to become the target.
chosen.visualIdea: Show Electabuzz racing up tall trees as lightning targets appear above competing Pokémon.
chosen.note: A highly specific, strange behavior backed by multiple entries: Electabuzz competes to climb lightning-prone heights, waits for strikes, and is used by some towns as a lightning rod.

candidates.premise: When two Electabuzz touch, they control electric currents to communicate their feelings.
candidates.hook: Electabuzz can talk through electricity—but only when it touches another one.
candidates.visualIdea: Two Electabuzz touch, sending colored current patterns between them that resolve into emotion symbols.
candidates.note: Very Pokémon-specific and visually clear. The research supports communication through electric currents when two Electabuzz touch, though the hook's implication that touching is required is slightly stronger than the cited wording.

candidates.premise: Electabuzz evolves from Elekid at level 30, then needs a trade while holding an Electirizer to evolve again.
candidates.hook: Electabuzz’s next evolution requires a trade—and a specific held item.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Elekid becoming Electabuzz at level 30, then a trade animation with Electirizer before Electivire appears.
candidates.note: Accurate and easy to visualize, but trade evolutions and held-item requirements are less surprising than Electabuzz's storm behavior.

candidates.premise: Electabuzz eats electricity, but it leaks electricity in amounts far greater than what it consumes.
candidates.hook: Electabuzz is an electricity eater that gives off even more than it eats.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate electricity flowing into Electabuzz, then show an even larger current bursting back out.
candidates.note: Excellent contradiction and visual hook, but the cited indices point to blackout and charging entries rather than the Moon entry stating that Electabuzz leaks more electricity than it eats.

candidates.premise: Electabuzz windmills its arms to slightly boost a punch, but opponents can escape during the windup.
candidates.hook: Electabuzz powers up its punch long enough for the opponent to run away.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Electabuzz spinning its arms faster while an opponent calmly exits the frame.
candidates.note: The comic premise is strong, but the cited indices do not contain the windmill-punch entry or the matching charging description.

candidates.premise: Electabuzz is blamed for blackouts, but one Pokédex entry says electric-company errors cause them more often.
candidates.hook: Electabuzz might be innocent of the blackouts it gets blamed for.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Electabuzz beside a blackout headline, then reveal an electric-company error stamp.
candidates.note: The premise is distinctive and supported by the research in general, but the cited evidence indices do not point to the blackout-blame and electric-company-error entries.

rounds.request: Stronger alternatives would need equally concrete, Pokémon-specific behavior with correctly matched evidence citations; the electricity-leak angle is especially promising if its citation is corrected to the Moon entry.
